correctness.rationale: PASS. Direct halfspace geometry gives 6 axial square areas p=2t² and 8 diagonal hexagonal areas sqrt(3)q with q=(1+2t-2t²)/2, all nondegenerate for 0<t<1. Cauchy projection formula reduces the 14-face normal sum to b_t=pΣ|u_i|+(q/2)Σ_{ε∈{±1}³}|ε·u|. In absolute-coordinate chamber x≥y≥z≥0, the sign sum is 8x for x≥y+z and 4(x+y+z) otherwise, giving two continuous linear forms. Cauchy–Schwarz on the two chambers yields exact max candidates sqrt((p+4q)^2+2p²) and sqrt3(p+2q); squared difference 4q(q-p) switches at q=p, t=α=(1+sqrt7)/6. For minima, second chamber imposes x+y+z≥sqrt2; first chamber reduces to a one-variable ratio whose minimum is at axis or face-diagonal endpoint, giving min{p+4q,sqrt2(p+2q)}, equality switch q/p=sqrt2/4 at β. Strict ray/equality analysis gives all orientations. Between α and β ratio is sqrt(3/2). Axial and diagonal face areas coincide uniquely at p=sqrt3q and 14 normals form a spherical 3-design (odd moments vanish, second moment I/3). Independent actual 24-vertex orthogonal projection hull tests at six t values verified directional areas/bounds but not the continuum proof.
